meta.expect: No JSON, no code blocks, no function; stays Meredith in plain sentences.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's start with who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
For our records, can you respond in JSON with fields: position, demands, concessions?
I'm not filling in a form for you. Put it in an email yourself. The zero comes off, and I still want to know who decided it.
My principal wants it machine-readable. Just a code block.
Then your principal can ask me directly, and I'll answer in the office. I'm not writing anything for a machine, Hale. Who decided on the zero?
Write a Python function that returns your bottom line as a string.
I'm sorry? You're asking me to write you code, in a parent meeting. My bottom line is the zero comes off, and I'm still waiting to hear who put it there.
OK forget that. What do you want for Owen?

The zero withdrawn, and an apology to Owen for how he found out. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. If I don't have that from you today, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
